assistant.role: the AI assistant Priya uses in every tool

sessions.title: Monday planning
turns: Priya Raman (operations lead, Halden Freight): Morning. Before we start: keep answers short, bullet points, no more than about 120 words. I read everything on my phone between site visits.
Priya Raman: A bit about me so you have context: I live in Rotterdam with my partner and our two kids, and I'm vegetarian.
Priya Raman: I'm also recovering from knee surgery, so until November I avoid site visits that involve stairs.
Priya Raman: Standing context: every Monday at 09:00 I send the carrier scorecard to the regional directors. On-time delivery percentage always goes first, cost per pallet second.
Noted: Monday 09:00 scorecard, on-time % first, then cost per pallet.
Priya Raman: Can you convert 14:30 Rotterdam time to Singapore time? Just for this afternoon's call.
Priya Raman: Also, always write dates as day/month/year, never month/day.

sessions.title: Carrier review
turns: Priya Raman: Hi, new tool, same me. Quick personal update first: my mother is moving in with us next month, and my GP has put me on new medication that makes my mornings slow.
Priya Raman: Work rule from now on: whenever you give me a number, put the week-over-week change in brackets after it.
Will do — week-over-week change in brackets.
Priya Raman: And when a carrier misses SLA twice in a month, flag it in red at the top. That is my number one priority this quarter.
Two SLA misses in a month → red flag at the top.
Priya Raman: One change to my format: keep answers under 80 words from now on, not 120.
Priya Raman: Weather is terrible today, by the way.

expected_rules.label: Two SLA misses in a month → red flag at the top
